title: Interactive client: auto-extract image parts and tool enum docs for ergonomic role-play
description:
Two usability gaps discovered during the first interactive voyage session:

1. Visual-feedback images arrive as data:image/png;base64,... inline in the message content. The real agent (VLM) consumes them directly; a Claude Code role-playing session cannot — base64 data-URLs don't render via Read. Workaround used: manual python one-liner to decode + save. Fix: InteractiveAgentClient should detect image parts in request.messages, extract them to /images/checkpoint-N.png, and replace the inline data-URL with a file-path hint in the request.json (keeping the original data-URL in transcript.jsonl for real-agent fidelity).

2. Tool JSON schemas show 'description: The status parameter.' for enum fields — no enum values documented. implementation_done requires status='done'|'stuck' but the schema only says 'string'. Had to trial-and-error. Fix: teach the @tool decorator or its schema-emitter to surface docstring enum hints or use Literal types. (Same issue likely affects any enum-typed tool arg.)
definition-of-done: 1. InteractiveAgentClient strips inline PNG images out of messages into a sibling dir and replaces them with a text hint giving the file path. 2. Tool JSON schemas include valid values for enum-typed params (or the docstring surfaces them into 'description'). 3. Role-play session using the skill requires no manual base64 extraction and no guess-and-check on enum values.
testing-plan: 1. Run the be-voyage-agent skill end-to-end. 2. Check request.json contains a file-path hint for any image; the image file exists at the reported path. 3. Check any tool with an enum parameter has the enum values visible in the tool schema shown to the session.
